Project-specific Copilot instructions
===============================

Summary
-------
- Small React + Vite demo that targets WebXR using `@react-three/fiber`, `@react-three/xr`, and `three`.
- Key UX: a single, in-world UI for entering XR and interacting with an animated GLB model.

Architecture & important patterns
--------------------------------
- Entry: `src/main.jsx` mounts a single React tree (no `StrictMode`) because WebXR/session init is sensitive to double-mounts.
- App-level: `src/App.jsx` creates a single XR store via `createXRStore({ offerSession: false })` and passes it to the VR entry UI and the `<XR>` canvas.
- Rendering: `src/components/XRCanvas.jsx` wraps a `@react-three/fiber` `<Canvas>` with `@react-three/xr`'s `<XR>` so Three controls the render loop and controllers/hand inputs are mounted by the library.
- Model: `src/components/Model.jsx` loads `src/models/machine.glb` (generated by `scripts/generate-machine-glb.mjs`) and exposes animation clip names via `useAnimations` → `onAnimationNames` callback.
- Controls: `src/components/XRControls.jsx` renders in-world interactive buttons (uses `Interactive` from `@react-three/xr`) rather than DOM overlays so controls work inside headsets.

Developer workflows (commands)
------------------------------
- Start dev server with HMR: `npm run dev` (or `npm run dev:host` to expose to LAN).
- Build: `npm run build` and preview with `npm run preview`.
- Regenerate placeholder GLB: `npm run generate:model` (runs `scripts/generate-machine-glb.mjs` and outputs `src/models/machine.glb`).

Conventions & gotchas
---------------------
- Keep React tree single-mounted for predictable WebXR lifecycle. Do not wrap `App` in `React.StrictMode` here.
- XR store patterns: the app creates one store and passes it to both the VR button and the `<XR>` provider; do not create multiple stores.
- Place in-world UI near eye level and slightly forward — `XRControls` uses `[0, 1.35, -1.0]` and the model is placed at `[0, 0, -1.5]` to ensure visibility in headset.
- Desktop fallbacks: input handlers often include both `onSelect` (XR) and `onClick` (desktop mouse). Preserve both when editing controls.
- Assets: the repo generates a tiny, animated GLB for demos — replace `src/models/machine.glb` with your real model if needed. See `scripts/generate-machine-glb.mjs` for how the placeholder is created.

Files to inspect for common changes
----------------------------------
- App / XR wiring: `src/App.jsx` and `src/components/XRCanvas.jsx`
- Model loading & clips: `src/components/Model.jsx`
- In-world controls: `src/components/XRControls.jsx` and `src/components/EnterXR.jsx`
- Dev scripts & assets: `scripts/generate-machine-glb.mjs`, `package.json` scripts

When making PRs
---------------
- Run `npm run lint` and `npm run dev` locally; test both desktop and an immersive device (or the browser's WebXR emulation).
- Keep `offerSession: false` behavior: users must click to enter XR. If you change session offer behavior, document why.

Examples (copy-paste)
---------------------
- Create the XR store (App.jsx):

```js
const xrStore = useMemo(() => createXRStore({ offerSession: false }), [])
```

- Load model (Model.jsx) and forward animation names:

```js
const { actions, names } = useAnimations(gltf.animations, group)
useEffect(() => onAnimationNames?.(names ?? []), [onAnimationNames, names])
```

If anything here is unclear or you want more automation (tests, CI rules, or expanded examples), tell me which area to expand.
